binary.note: ABI Version field in ELF header is 65 (non-standard), causing ldd to report 'ELF file ABI version invalid' and 'not a dynamic executable'. Binary runs normally despite this.

relro.note: No RELRO segment. .got and .got.plt are both writable (WA flags). No BIND_NOW in dynamic section.

canary.note: No __stack_chk_fail in symbols/GOT. No canary-related instructions observed in disassembly.

pie.note: ELF type EXEC, base address 0x400000. Not position-independent.

ibt.note: No GNU_PROPERTY note with IBT flag.

shstk.note: No GNU_PROPERTY note with SHSTK flag.

aslr.note: PIE is disabled so binary base is fixed at 0x400000. Library ASLR depends on kernel/system config, not confirmed.

libc.note: Version requirements from .gnu.version_r. Actual libc path cannot be resolved via ldd due to ABI Version=65. System ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 is the interpreter.

libraries.name: libdl.so.2
libraries.note: ldd fails due to ABI version. Standard system path expected.

libraries.name: libpthread.so.0
libraries.note: ldd fails due to ABI version.

libraries.name: libz.so.1
libraries.note: ldd fails due to ABI version. Used for uncompress().

libraries.name: libc.so.6
libraries.note: ldd fails due to ABI version.

libraries.name: libnotify.so.3 through libnotify.so.8
libraries.note: NOT in NEEDED. Loaded at runtime via dlopen() in notify() function (0x404800). Tries .so.3 first, falls back to .so.8. No RPATH/RUNPATH so LD_LIBRARY_PATH takes priority over system paths.

libraries.name: libfuse.so.2
libraries.note: NOT in NEEDED. Loaded at runtime via dlopen() in main() at 0x405be8 with RTLD_LAZY. Stored in global libhandle (0x62af90). No RPATH/RUNPATH so LD_LIBRARY_PATH takes priority.

rpath.note: No DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH in .dynamic section. Library search order: LD_LIBRARY_PATH > /etc/ld.so.cache > default paths. External libraries (libnotify.so.*, libfuse.so.2) can be hijacked by placing them in LD_LIBRARY_PATH or CWD if set.

input_sources.description: Command-line arguments parsed in main(). Uses getArg() to find options like --appimage-version, --appimage-offset, --appimage-help, --appimage-extract-and-run.
TARGET_APPIMAGE env var used in main() at 0x4054a4 (getenv) and build_mount_point() at 0x405403. APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN env var checked. APPIMAGE env var used for path construction.
stdin FILE* accessed in notify() at 0x404800 via fileno() for isatty() check.

functions.name: main@@Base
checks: getenv(TARGET_APPIMAGE) != NULL ? use env value : use argv[0] (0x4054a9-0x4054c3)

memory_operations.description: Copies TARGET_APPIMAGE or argv[0] to stack buffer at [rbp-0x6030]. No length check. Buffer is 0x1000 bytes from rbp-0x6030 to rbp-0x5030.
Copies getenv(APPIMAGE) result to [rbp-0x5030]. No length check.
Copies getenv(APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN) result to [rbp-0x4030] if set. No length check. Buffer initialized with rep stos (0x3fe dwords = 0xff8 bytes).
Stores dlopen('libfuse.so.2', RTLD_LAZY) return value to libhandle global at 0x405bf5.
Sets have_libloaded=1 after successful dlopen at 0x405c20.

functions.name: mkdir_p@@Base
checks: strlen(path) <= 0xfff (4095) via cmp rbp,0xfff; jbe (0x404d3a-0x404d4a). If > 4095, sets errno=ENAMETOOLONG (0x24) and returns -1.

memory_operations.description: Copies input path to 4104-byte stack buffer via strcpy at 0x404d5f. The length check only rejects paths > 4095 bytes, but the buffer is 4104 bytes. Paths of length 4096-4103 pass the check and are copied. However, strcpy adds a null terminator, so paths of exactly 4096-4103 bytes would write 4097-4104 bytes into the 4104-byte buffer, which fits. Paths of 4104+ bytes are rejected by the check. The off-by-one: the check uses <= 4095 (jbe), but the buffer is 4104 bytes, so there is a gap of 8 bytes where paths pass the check but are close to the buffer boundary.

strlen(basename_result) compared to 6, uses min(strlen, 6) for strncpy (0x404421-0x40443b)

Writes 'XXXXXX' (0x58585858 + 0x5858) at dest_buf+rbx+8 at 0x40546b-0x405471. Null-terminates at dest_buf+rbx+0xe.

attack_surfaces.operation: strcpy to stack [rbp-0x6030] and [rbp-0x5030] without length check
attack_surfaces.reason: Attacker-controlled environment variable (TARGET_APPIMAGE, APPIMAGE) is copied via strcpy to fixed-size stack buffers (0x1000 bytes each, from rbp-0x6030 to rbp-0x5030 and rbp-0x5030 to rbp-0x4030) without any length validation. No stack canary present. Environment variables can be arbitrarily long. This is a direct attacker-controlled value reaching an unbounded strcpy on a stack buffer with no canary.

attack_surfaces.operation: strcpy to stack [rbp-0x4030] without length check
attack_surfaces.reason: getenv(APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN) result is strcpy'd to [rbp-0x4030] at 0x405535. Buffer was initialized with rep stos of 0x3fe dwords (0xff8 bytes). No length check on the env var value. No canary.

attack_surfaces.input: path argument (from extract_appimage, derived from user-controlled env/argv)
attack_surfaces.operation: strcpy to 4104-byte stack buffer with boundary check at 4095
attack_surfaces.reason: Stack buffer is 0x1008 (4104) bytes but check rejects only paths > 4095 bytes (cmp rbp,0xfff; jbe). Paths of length 4096-4103 pass the check. strcpy writes strlen+1 bytes. For path length 4103, strcpy writes 4104 bytes which exactly fills the buffer. For path length 4104+, the check rejects. The off-by-one between check (4095) and buffer (4104) creates a window, but overflow beyond the buffer requires path length >= 4104 which is rejected. The actual risk depends on whether the 8-byte gap (4096-4103) can be exploited given the buffer is at rsp (not rbp) and the function frame is small.

attack_surfaces.operation: strcpy to caller-provided buffer without length check
attack_surfaces.reason: getenv(TARGET_APPIMAGE) or basename(argv[0]) result is strcpy'd to caller-provided buffer at 0x40543f with no length validation. The buffer size depends on the caller (main). If main's stack buffer is the destination, this is the same unbounded strcpy pattern. Additionally, strncpy at 0x405461 copies basename result with length min(strlen, 6), which is bounded.

attack_surfaces.operation: malloc(strlen) + strcpy + strcat with potential off-by-one in allocation
attack_surfaces.reason: malloc(strlen(dest_dir)) allocates exactly strlen bytes (not strlen+1 for null terminator) at 0x404e65. strcpy at 0x404e77 writes strlen+1 bytes (including null). Then if path doesn't end with '/', strcat appends '/' adding another byte. This is a 1-2 byte heap overflow (off-by-one/off-by-two) on a heap buffer. No canary on heap. Could corrupt heap metadata.

notify() calls dlopen('libnotify.so.3', RTLD_NOW=1) at 0x404856, falling back to .so.4-.so.8 at 0x40494c. No RPATH/RUNPATH in binary. LD_LIBRARY_PATH takes priority over system paths. Attacker can place malicious libnotify.so.3 in LD_LIBRARY_PATH or CWD to hijack library loading. dlsym resolves notify_init, notify_notification_new, notify_notification_show, notify_notification_set_timeout, notify_notification_close which are then called indirectly. No RELRO means GOT is also writable.

attack_surfaces.operation: dlopen with RTLD_LAZY, stored in writable global libhandle
attack_surfaces.reason: main() calls dlopen('libfuse.so.2', RTLD_LAZY=1) at 0x405bed, stores result in global libhandle (0x62af90, in .bss, writable). No RPATH/RUNPATH. LD_LIBRARY_PATH takes priority. Attacker can hijack libfuse.so.2 loading. fusefs_main() then uses dlsym on libhandle to resolve fuse functions and calls them indirectly. No RELRO means GOT entries for dlopen/dlsym themselves are writable.

sprintf at 0x404def writes to a 0x20 (32) byte stack buffer. If the format string produces output > 32 bytes, stack buffer overflow occurs. No canary. The format string is at 0x421678 and arguments come from caller. Need to verify format string content and argument controllability.

attack_surfaces.function: sqfs_open_image@@Base and related squashfs parsing functions
attack_surfaces.operation: fread/pread of attacker-controlled file format data
attack_surfaces.reason: Processes squashfs filesystem image embedded in AppImage. Reads superblock, inode table, directory entries from file. Attacker can craft malformed squashfs image with manipulated sizes/offsets. Potential for integer overflows or heap corruption during parsing. Requires detailed analysis of sqfs_* functions.

attack_surfaces.operation: GOT entries are writable (WA permissions on .got and .got.plt)
attack_surfaces.reason: No RELRO protection. Both .got (0x62ab20, WA) and .got.plt (0x62ab78, WA) are writable. Any write primitive can overwrite GOT entries to hijack control flow. dlopen, dlsym, strcpy, execv, fork, system-related entries are all in writable GOT. This is a fact about the binary's protection profile, not a vulnerability by itself.

facts.description: Binary is ELF64 EXEC, x86-64, little-endian, dynamically linked, stripped. Entry point 0x404690. Interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2.
ABI Version field in ELF header is 65 (non-standard). This causes ldd to fail with 'ELF file ABI version invalid' and 'not a dynamic executable'. Binary still runs normally.
No RELRO: no GNU_RELRO segment, no BIND_NOW in .dynamic. .got (0x62ab20, WA) and .got.plt (0x62ab78, WA) are both writable.
No stack canary: no __stack_chk_fail in symbols/GOT, no canary instructions in disassembly.
No PIE: ELF type EXEC, base 0x400000. All addresses are fixed.
NX enabled: GNU_STACK segment has RW permissions (no X).
No FORTIFY: no __*_chk functions in GOT/PLT.
No CET (IBT/SHSTK): no GNU_PROPERTY notes with IBT or SHSTK flags.
Dynamic dependencies (NEEDED): libdl.so.2, libpthread.so.0, libz.so.1, libc.so.6. No RPATH or RUNPATH in .dynamic section.

libnotify.so.3 through libnotify.so.8 are NOT in NEEDED. They are loaded at runtime via dlopen() in notify() function (0x404800). Tries .so.3 first (0x404856), falls back sequentially to .so.8 (0x40494c).
libfuse.so.2 is NOT in NEEDED. Loaded at runtime via dlopen('libfuse.so.2', RTLD_LAZY=1) in main() at 0x405bed. Result stored in global libhandle (0x62af90).

main() at 0x405485 uses sub rsp,0x6438 (25,656 bytes) for stack frame. Stack buffers: [rbp-0x6030] (0x1000 bytes), [rbp-0x5030] (0x1000 bytes), [rbp-0x4030] (0xff8 bytes initialized), [rbp-0x1030] (0x1000 bytes for readlink).
main() copies getenv(TARGET_APPIMAGE) or argv[0] to [rbp-0x6030] via strcpy at 0x4054ba/0x4054d9. No length check. Buffer is 0x1000 bytes.
main() copies getenv(APPIMAGE) to [rbp-0x5030] via strcpy at 0x4054f2. No length check.
main() copies getenv(APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN) to [rbp-0x4030] via strcpy at 0x405535 if env var is set. No length check. Buffer initialized with 0x3fe dwords (0xff8 bytes).
mkdir_p() at 0x404d10 allocates 0x1008 (4104) bytes on stack (sub rsp,0x1008). Length check: cmp rbp,0xfff (4095); jbe. Rejects paths > 4095 bytes. Copies path via strcpy to stack buffer at rsp.

build_mount_point() at 0x4053ea uses strcpy at 0x40543f to copy getenv(TARGET_APPIMAGE) or basename(argv[0]) to caller-provided buffer. No length check. Uses strncpy at 0x405461 with length min(strlen(basename), 6) for a second copy.

extract_appimage() at 0x404e1c: malloc(strlen(dest_dir)) at 0x404e65 (allocates strlen bytes, not strlen+1). strcpy at 0x404e77 writes strlen+1 bytes. strcat at 0x404e99 may add 1 more byte if path doesn't end with '/'. Potential 1-2 byte heap overflow.
portable_option() at 0x404dd4 uses sprintf to 0x20 (32) byte stack buffer at 0x404def. Format string at 0x421678.

Binary is AppImageKit runtime. Contains squashfs extraction (extract_appimage, sqfs_open_image at 0x40a502), FUSE mounting (fusefs_main at 0x40dfcc), and AppImage ELF offset calculation (appimage_get_elf_size at 0x405fe0).
Binary runs normally: --appimage-version outputs 'effcebc', --appimage-offset outputs '188392', --appimage-help prints help text.
Global variable libhandle at 0x62af90 (.bss, 8 bytes) stores dlopen handle for libfuse.so.2. Written at 0x405bf5 in main(). have_libloaded at 0x62aee0 set to 1 at 0x405c20 after successful dlopen.
GOT contains 82 JUMP_SLOT entries and 7 GLOB_DAT entries, all in writable .got/.got.plt sections. Key entries: dlopen@0x62ad68, dlsym@0x62ad88, strcpy@0x62ad38, execv@0x62abb8, fork@0x62ada0.

Library search order with no RPATH/RUNPATH: LD_LIBRARY_PATH > /etc/ld.so.cache > default system paths (/lib, /usr/lib). Both NEEDED libraries and dlopen'd libraries (libnotify.so.*, libfuse.so.2) follow this order.

notify() calls dlsym on dlopen'd libnotify handle to resolve: notify_init (0x420f7e), AppImage (0x420f8a), notify_notification_new (0x420f93), notify_notification_show (0x420fc8), notify_notification_set_timeout (0x420fab), notify_notification_close (0x420fd0). These are called indirectly via call rax.

main() stack layout: sub rsp,0x6438. Buffers at rbp-0x6030 (path), rbp-0x5030 (appimage), rbp-0x4030 (extract_and_run), rbp-0x1030 (readlink), rbp-0x750 (sqfs context). Adjacent buffers with no canary between them.

uncertainties.description: Actual libc version and path cannot be resolved via ldd due to ABI Version=65 in ELF header.
uncertainties.reason: ldd reports 'ELF file ABI version invalid' and 'not a dynamic executable'. The binary still runs, suggesting the runtime linker tolerates the non-standard ABI version, but ldd does not.

uncertainties.description: Whether the strcpy of TARGET_APPIMAGE/APPIMAGE env vars to stack buffers in main() is reachable in a context where the attacker controls these environment variables.
uncertainties.reason: Environment variable control depends on the execution context (setuid binary, service, etc.). The binary itself does not appear to be setuid. Need S2 to determine threat model.

uncertainties.description: Whether mkdir_p's off-by-one gap (check at 4095, buffer at 4104) is exploitable.
uncertainties.reason: Paths of length 4096-4103 pass the check and are strcpy'd to the 4104-byte buffer. strcpy writes strlen+1 bytes (4097-4104), which fits within the buffer. Paths >= 4104 are rejected. The gap may not produce an actual overflow beyond the buffer. Need S2 to analyze exact boundary behavior.

uncertainties.description: Whether extract_appimage's malloc(strlen) + strcpy + strcat produces an exploitable heap overflow.
uncertainties.reason: malloc allocates strlen bytes, strcpy writes strlen+1 (1 byte overflow for null terminator), strcat may add 1 more byte. This is a 1-2 byte heap off-by-one. Exploitability depends on heap implementation and adjacent chunk layout. Need S2/S3 to assess.

uncertainties.description: Content of format string at 0x421678 used by portable_option's sprintf.
uncertainties.reason: Need to read .rodata at this address to determine if sprintf output can exceed 32 bytes. The format string and argument controllability need S2 analysis.

uncertainties.description: Full extent of squashfs parsing attack surface.
uncertainties.reason: sqfs_open_image and related sqfs_* functions process complex filesystem image format. Detailed analysis of all sqfs_* functions (inode parsing, directory traversal, data block reading) is needed to identify integer overflows or heap corruption. Only sqfs_open_image entry point was examined.

uncertainties.description: Whether the binary is typically invoked in a context where environment variables or CWD are attacker-controlled.
uncertainties.reason: The dlopen library hijacking attack requires the attacker to control LD_LIBRARY_PATH or place libraries in the search path. This depends on the deployment context (desktop shortcut, service, script wrapper, etc.).
PIE is disabled (binary base fixed at 0x400000), but library ASLR depends on kernel configuration which was not confirmed. If ASLR is disabled, library addresses are predictable.
